title: Merge Strings Alternately
statement:
You are given two non-empty strings `a` and `b` of lowercase English letters. Build a new string by interleaving them: take the first character of `a`, then the first character of `b`, then the second character of `a`, then the second character of `b`, and so on.

If one string is longer than the other, the characters that are left over after the shorter string runs out are appended to the end of the result unchanged. Print the merged string.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the string `a`.
The second line contains the string `b`.
constraints: `a` and `b` consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Alternate while both have letters: s, m, u, o, n, o. Now `a` is used up, so the leftover "n" of `b` is appended.
Equal lengths: a, c, b, d.
h, x, e, y are interleaved, then the leftover "llo" of `a` is appended.

hints: Use one index (or two pointers) that walks through both strings at the same time.
While the index is inside a string, append that string's character; do `a` first, then `b`.
Once the shorter string ends, keep going: the same loop naturally appends the remaining characters of the longer one.
